title: Bereshit: one person, a whole world
hookLine: one human was created first, the Mishnah says, to teach that one life is a whole world (Sanhedrin 4:5)
tomorrow: Bereshit: you can rule over it

lines: A COURTROOM, A LIFE AT STAKE.
THE JUDGES TAKE THE WITNESSES ASIDE.
cards: A courtroom, as the Mishnah describes it. A life is at stake: the charge carries the death penalty. Before the witnesses speak, the judges take them aside.

They don't just say, tell the truth. They make them sit through a short lesson from the book of Genesis, about why God began the human race with just one person. Today, the lesson those witnesses heard.

teach.h: ONE LIFE IS A WHOLE WORLD.
teach.b: It's in the Mishnah, tractate Sanhedrin. Why was the first human created alone? The Mishnah gives several answers.
First: whoever destroys a single life, scripture counts it as if they destroyed a whole world. And whoever sustains a single life, as if they sustained a whole world.
Adam was one person, and from him came everyone, so every single person carries a whole world inside. Second: for the sake of peace.

teach.h: NO ONE CAN SAY MY FATHER IS GREATER.
teach.b: Since everyone comes from one ancestor, no one can say, my father is greater than yours. Third: to show God's greatness.

teach.h: ONE MOLD, AND NO TWO ALIKE.
teach.b: When a person stamps coins from one mold, the Mishnah says, they all come out alike. But God stamped every human from the mold of the first, and not one is like another. Then the Mishnah draws a startling conclusion.

teach.h: FOR MY SAKE THE WORLD WAS CREATED.
teach.b: Each person is obligated to say: for my sake the world was created.
Later teachers read that not as arrogance but as responsibility: if the world was made for you, you're answerable for it. And if it was made for them too, every person you meet is a whole world.
That's what the witnesses were meant to feel. You're not testifying about a case. You're holding a world in your hands.

how: Jews often quote Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5, that saving one life is like saving a whole world, when teaching about human dignity, medicine and the value of every person.

o: in the beginning, the first word of Genesis
the six days of creation, taken together
the Hebrew name for the book of Exodus

games.q: why one person first — tap the pairs.
p: no one says my father is greater
for my sake the world was created

s: the Mishnah sets this lesson in a warning to witnesses in a capital case
the judges warned them with it before they testified.
the Mishnah says only kings may say the world was created for them
it says each person is obligated to say it.
the Mishnah gives only one reason for creating one person first
it gives several: a whole world, peace between people, and God's greatness.

games.q: you're a judge in the ancient court. witnesses are about to testify in a case where a life is at stake. what do you do first?
o: teach them why the first human was created alone.
ask them to swear on a scroll.
games.why: the Mishnah says the judges warned them with this lesson: one life is a whole world. testimony is holding a world in your hands.

practice: Bring to mind someone you'll see today, maybe someone you usually barely notice: a cashier, a neighbor, a coworker.
Picture everything inside them: their childhood, the people they love, what they're afraid of, what they hope for this year. Stay a minute with that world, as full as yours.

wordCard.voice: Bereshit. The first portion, where one human is created first, to teach that each life is a whole world.

orig.note: Hebrew: a full world, the Mishnah's phrase for a single life.

carryVoice: Your line: each life a world. Every one of them, yours included. That's day one hundred sixty-three.
